papers.title: Active Learning from Imperfect Labelers
papers.abstract: We study active learning where the labeler can not only return incorrect labels but also abstain from labeling. We consider different noise and abstention conditions of the labeler. We propose an algorithm which utilizes abstention responses, and analyze its statistical consistency and query complexity under fairly natural assumptions on the noise and abstention rate of the labeler. This algorithm is adaptive in a sense that it can automatically request less queries with a more informed or less noisy labeler. We couple our algorithm with lower bounds to show that under some technical conditions, it achieves nearly optimal query complexity.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关于含噪声标注者的主动学习，与有限元代理建模或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on theoretical active learning with noisy labels and abstention, with no application to FEA surrogate modeling, expensive simulation sampling, or biomechanical design.

summary_zh.motivation: 处理标注者可能出错或弃权的情况下的主动学习
summary_zh.method: 提出一种自适应算法，利用弃权响应并分析噪声条件
summary_zh.result: 算法在合理假设下达到近乎最优的查询复杂度
summary_zh.validation: 理论证明一致性与最优性

summary_en.motivation: To handle active learning scenarios where labelers may provide incorrect labels or abstain from labeling.
summary_en.method: An adaptive algorithm that utilizes abstention responses and is analyzed under natural noise and abstention assumptions.
summary_en.result: The algorithm achieves nearly optimal query complexity under certain technical conditions.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical proofs of statistical consistency and lower bounds on query complexity.

papers.title: Auxiliary gradient-based sampling algorithms
papers.abstract: We introduce a new family of MCMC samplers that combine auxiliary variables, Gibbs sampling and Taylor expansions of the target density. Our approach permits the marginalisation over the auxiliary variables yielding marginal samplers, or the augmentation of the auxiliary variables, yielding auxiliary samplers. The well-known Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm (MALA) and preconditioned Crank-Nicolson Langevin (pCNL) algorithm are shown to be special cases. We prove that marginal samplers are superior in terms of asymptotic variance and demonstrate cases where they are slower in computing time compared to auxiliary samplers. In the context of latent Gaussian models we propose new auxiliary and marginal samplers whose implementation requires a single tuning parameter, which can be found automatically during the transient phase. Extensive experimentation shows that the increase in efficiency (measured as effective sample size per unit of computing time) relative to (optimised implementations of) pCNL, elliptical slice sampling and MALA ranges from 10-fold in binary classification problems to 25-fold in log-Gaussian Cox processes to 100-fold in Gaussian process regression, and it is on par with Riemann manifold Hamiltonian Monte Carlo in an example where the latter has the same complexity as the aforementioned algorithms. We explain this remarkable improvement in terms of the way alternative samplers try to approximate the eigenvalues of the target. We introduce a novel MCMC sampling scheme for hyperparameter learning that builds upon the auxiliary samplers. The MATLAB code for reproducing the experiments in the article is publicly available and a Supplement to this article contains additional experiments and implementation details.

llm.relevance_to_user: 提出高效MCMC采样方法，可迁移至代理模型的不确定性量化，但未直接涉及有限元或生物力学。
llm.why_not_core: No application to FEA surrogate modeling, no biomechanics or implant context, only abstract statistical benchmarks.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高梯度基MCMC采样算法的效率。
summary_zh.method: 提出辅助变量与吉布斯采样及泰勒展开结合的梯度采样器。
summary_zh.result: 新方法在潜高斯模型上比标准方法效率提升10-100倍。
summary_zh.validation: 在分类、Cox过程、高斯过程回归等基准上比较验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve the sampling efficiency of gradient-based MCMC algorithms for Bayesian inference.
summary_en.method: Proposes a family of auxiliary gradient-based samplers combining Gibbs sampling and Taylor expansions of the target density.
summary_en.result: The new samplers achieve 10- to 100-fold improvements in effective sample size per unit time over standard methods on latent Gaussian models.
summary_en.validation: Empirical evaluation on benchmarks including binary classification, log-Gaussian Cox processes, and Gaussian process regression.
